The use of a combination of general anesthetic (propofol) and regional anesthetic (spinal anesthesia) was the most effective in reducing the incidence of acute pain after lower limb (below-knee) amputation.

the use of spinal anesthesia in patients with phantom pain following amputation is associated with a significant reduction in the intensity of pain, and that the use of a combination of spinal and general anesthesia is associated with a greater reduction in phantom pain intensity.

the incidence of phantom pain is high, and that phantom pain is more common and more severe after below-knee amputation than after above-knee amputation. 1 Phantom limb pain is one of the most common and debilitating pain syndromes in amputees.
